turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let me know if I am too quiet.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: You are fine, thank you for asking.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: I drove her over, I will listen along.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How can I help you today?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Something is wrong with my chest, I think.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does it move into your arms or up toward your neck?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I feel it in my jaw sometimes.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: When did you first notice it?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: This morning, while I was making tea.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What kind of sensation is it?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It is more of a dull ache.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does doing chores around the house set it off?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I missed that, can you repeat it?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let me say that again, facing you. Do you notice it when you exercise or exert yourself?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Only when I hurry.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does anything ease the pain when it is there?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Nothing really helps.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Are you drenched or clammy during the episodes?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A little sweaty, yes.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you felt faint or dizzy?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you feel winded along with the pain?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No trouble breathing at all.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let me ask about risk factors: tobacco, blood pressure, diabetes, cholesterol.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I have high blood pressure, and I have high cholesterol. I quit smoking years ago.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any heart problems in your close relatives?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My brother had bypass surgery.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you have a history of heart surgery or stents?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I have never had any.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Which pills do you take regularly?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I take Lisinopril and Atorvastatin.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: To finish, here is the plan. First, see the heart specialist within two weeks. Second, call 911 if the pain gets worse or does not stop. Can you repeat the plan in your own words for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I will see the heart specialist in two weeks and call 911 if the pain gets worse or will not stop.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: I will write it down for her.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Anything else on your mind?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I did not catch most of what the nurse told me earlier.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thank you for saying so. I will speak slowly and write down the main points.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, that is everything for today. Take care.
